Tosafot on Bava Batra 70b:1:1.hebrew: סוף סוף כי א"ל נאנסו לאו שבועה בעי - תימה: למאי דמפרש ר"ת בהגוזל קמא (ב"ק דף קו. ושם) בשמעתא דהטוען טענת גנב בפקדון, דלא מיחייב שבועת שומרין אלא היכא דאיכא הודאה במקצת, היכי קאמר "לאו שבועה בעי"? אין ה"נ דלא מיחייב שבועה דאורייתא! ואין לומר: "לאו שבועה בעי" — שבועת היסת קאמר, דהיכי תיסק אדעתיה דרב עמרם דנאמן, דקאמר רב חסדא ליפטר אפילו משבועת היסת? ועוד, דאמר בפרק כל הנשבעין (שבועות דף מה:) גבי רמי בר חמא ורבא, מכלל דתרוייהו סברי: המפקיד אצל חבירו בעדים — אין צריך להחזיר לו בעדים; בשטר — צריך להחזיר לו בשטר. וצריך לפרש: וצריך להחזיר לו בשטר — אם אין רוצה לישבע, אבל בשבועה נאמן; כי היכי דלא תיקשי דרבא אדרבא. דרבא אמר לקמן דמהימן לומר "החזרתי לך" במיגו דנאנסו, דקאמר רבא הלכתא דנשבע וגובה מחצה. ואי בשבועת היסת איירי, היכי קאמר "בעדים א"צ להחזיר לו בעדים ומהימן לומר החזרתיו לך בלא שבועה"? הא לעולם בעי שבועת היסת! ואומר ר"ת דהך שבועה דהכא מדרבנן, ונתקנה קודם שבועת היסת, כמו ההיא דהכותב (כתובות דף פז:) דהפוגמת כתובתה ועד אחד מעידה שהיא פרועה, דקאמר התם דהויא שבועה דרבנן:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 70b:1:1.english: "Ultimately, when he says to him 'they were lost to circumstances beyond my control,' does he not require an oath?" - This is puzzling: According to what Rabbeinu Tam explains in the first chapter of Bava Kamma, "HaGozel" (Bava Kamma 106a, and there), in the passage about one who makes a thief-claim regarding a deposit — that one is liable to the oath of bailees only where there is a partial admission — how can [the Gemara] say, "Does he not require an oath?" Indeed, here too he is not liable to a Torah-level oath! And one cannot say that "does he not require an oath?" means the *hesset* oath (the rabbinic oath imposed on a defendant who denies a claim). For how could it enter Rav Amram's mind that he is believed, such that Rav Chisda says he should be exempt even from the *hesset* oath? Furthermore, it says in the chapter "Kol HaNishba'in" (Shevuot 45b), regarding Rami bar Chama and Rava, that by implication both of them hold: One who deposits with his fellow before witnesses — [the bailee] need not return it to him before witnesses; [if the deposit was made] by a document — he must return it to him by a document. And it must be explained: and he must return it to him by a document — if he is unwilling to take an oath, but with an oath he is believed. This is so that Rava will not be contradicted by Rava himself. For Rava says later that he is believed to say "I returned it to you," by virtue of the *migo* of [his being able to claim] "they were lost to circumstances beyond my control," since Rava said the halakhah is that he swears and collects half. But if [the Gemara] is speaking of the *hesset* oath, how can it say, "before witnesses, he need not return it to him before witnesses, and he is believed to say 'I returned it to you' without an oath"? Surely he always requires the *hesset* oath! Rabbeinu Tam says that this oath here is rabbinic, and it was enacted before the *hesset* oath, like the case in Ketubot (87b) of a woman who diminishes her *ketubah* [by admitting partial payment] and one witness testifies that it has been paid, where [the Gemara] says there that it is a rabbinic oath.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 70b:2:1.hebrew: נשבע וגובה מחצה - נראה דאינו נשבע על הכל, דלמה ישבע בחנם? כיון דאין משלמין לו אלא החצי, הלכך ישבע שבועה שיש לי בידם, ואין לי בידם פחות מחצי, דלא ליהוי מרע ליה לדיבוריה, כי ההיא דשנים אוחזין בטלית (ב"מ דף ה:):
Tosafot on Bava Batra 70b:2:1.english: He swears and collects half - It seems that he does not swear about the whole [amount], for why should he swear needlessly, since they pay him only half? Therefore, he swears an oath that "I have [this much] in their possession, and I do not have in their possession less than half," so that he not undermine his own statement, like that case of "two people holding a garment" (Bava Metzia 5b):

Tosafot on Bava Batra 70b:4:1.hebrew: מ"ד נשבע וגובה כולו לית ליה דרב חסדא - וא"ת: אכתי אמאי גובה כולו? דניטעון ליתמי "נאנסו"! וי"ל: דמלתא דלא שכיח היא, לא טענינן ליתמי דנאנסו; קלא אית ליה. ואע"ג דאבוהון הוי מהימן לומר שנאנסו, מיהו לא טענינן להו. ומאן דאמר נשבע וגובה מחצה סבר דלא מצי אמר ליה "שטרך בידי מאי בעי", וטענינן להו "החזרתיו לך", אף על גב דלא טענינן להו "נאנסו", כיון דאבוהון היה מהימן בטענה זו, מיגו דאי בעי אמר "נאנסו". ואין להקשות לרבי אבא דאית ליה "מתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם": אמאי פטרינן להו? הא מחויבין הן שבועה ואין יכולין לישבע! דלגבי יורשין לא אמרינן "מתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם", כדדרשינן בפ' כל הנשבעין (שבועות דף מז. ושם): "שבועת ה' תהיה בין שניהם" — ולא בין היורשין. ואם תאמר לרב ושמואל דקאמרי התם "אין אדם מוריש שבועה לבניו" — פי': אין אדם מוריש ממון שיש בו שבועה לבניו — אמאי פטורין מלשלם? וי"ל: דהא דאין אדם מוריש, היינו דאין נזקקין לא לשבועה ולא לפרעון, כדפירש הקונט' התם. ואם באין לגבות בשטר — אין גובין; אבל אם מוחזקין הן ובאין לגבות מהן כי הכא — אין מוציאין מהן, ופטורין. וכן מוכח בהדיא בפ' כל הנשבעין (שבועות דף מח:), דמשני: הא מני? ב"ש היא, דאמרי: שטר העומד לגבות כגבוי דמי; אלמא בדבר הגבוי אדם מוריש שבועה לבניו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 70b:4:1.english: The one who says he swears and collects the entire [debt] does not hold [the ruling] of Rav Chisda - And if you ask: Still, why does he collect all of it? Let us argue on behalf of the orphans that [the money] "was lost through circumstances beyond his control"! And one can answer: Since this is an uncommon occurrence, we do not argue on behalf of the orphans that [the money] was lost through circumstances beyond his control; it would have become publicly known. And although their father would have been believed to say that it was lost through circumstances beyond his control, nevertheless we do not argue this on their behalf. But the one who says he swears and collects half holds that [the debtor] cannot say, "What do I want with your document? It is in my hand," and we do argue on behalf of the orphans, "I returned it to you," even though we do not argue on their behalf that it was lost through circumstances beyond his control; since their father would have been believed with this claim, by virtue of a migo—that had he wished, he could have said, "It was lost through circumstances beyond his control." And one should not raise a difficulty against Rabbi Abba, who holds [the principle] "since he cannot swear, he pays": Why do we exempt them? Surely they are obligated to take an oath, and they cannot swear! [The answer is] that with regard to heirs we do not say "since he cannot swear, he pays," as we expound in the chapter [beginning] "Kol HaNishba'in" (Shevuot 47a, there): "The oath of the Lord shall be between the two of them"—and not between the heirs. And if you ask according to Rav and Shmuel, who say there, "A person does not bequeath an oath to his children"—meaning, a person does not bequeath to his children money that involves an oath—why are [the heirs] exempt from paying? And one can answer: That which "a person does not bequeath" means that we do not attend to them either for an oath or for payment, as the Kuntres [Rashi] explained there. So if they come to collect with a document, they do not collect; but if they are in possession and others come to collect from them, as here, [the money] is not taken out of their hands, and they are exempt. And so it is explicitly proven in the chapter "Kol HaNishba'in" (Shevuot 48b), where [the Gemara] answers: Whose view is this? It is Beit Shammai, who say: A document that is destined to be collected is considered as already collected; evidently, with regard to a collectible matter, a person does bequeath an oath to his children.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 70b:7:1.hebrew: דאם איתא דפרע מימר הוה אמר - דוקא הכא שיש שטר על בניו, היה לו להודיעם דפרוע הוא. אבל מלוה על פה, אמרינן דאין גובה מן היורשין, ואפילו הניח קרקעות ואפי' מגדולים, אלא כשהודה ומת, א"נ דשמתוהו ומית בשמתא. דהתם לא אמרינן "אם איתא דפרע מימר הוה אמר", דאין לו להודיעו כל מה שלוה ופרע כל ימי חייו; אלא דוקא הכא שיש שטר, כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 70b:7:1.english: "For if it were so that he had paid, he would have said so" - Specifically here, where there is a document against his sons, he should have informed them that it was paid. But [regarding] an oral loan, we say that it is not collected from the heirs, even if he left land, and even from adults, unless he admitted [the debt] and died, or [if] they excommunicated him and he died under excommunication. For there we do not say, "If it were so that he had paid, he would have said so," since he has no obligation to inform [his heirs] of everything that he borrowed and repaid throughout his life; rather, [this reasoning applies] specifically here, where there is a document, as I explained.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 70b:8:1.hebrew: אמר רבא הלכתא נשבע וגובה מחצה - ומה שקשה דרבא אדרבא, בשבועות פירשתי לעיל. וריב"ם מפרש דלא קשיא מידי, דהכי איתא התם: א"ל רבא: מאי מעלייתא? א"כ שבועת שומרין דחייב רחמנא, היכי משכחת לה? מתוך שיכול לומר "לא היו דברים מעולם" יכול לומר "נאנסו"! דאפקיד ליה בעדים. דאפקיד ליה בעדים נמי, מתוך שיכול לומר "החזרתי לך" יכול לומר "נאנסו"! דאפקיד ליה בשטר. פירוש: כיון דאפקיד ליה בשטר, איכא שבועה בנאנסו, דאז אין לומר "מתוך שיכול לומר 'החזרתיו לך'" והיה נאמן בלא שבועה, דהא המפקיד אצל חבירו בשטר צריך להחזיר לו בעדים; ומן הדין אפילו בשבועה לא היה נאמן, אי לאו משום דמהימן במיגו דנאנסו בשבועה. והשתא אין להקשות כלום משם:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 70b:8:1.english: Rava said: The halakha is that he swears and collects half - As for the difficulty raised from Rava's own statement [elsewhere], to the contrary — I explained this above in [tractate] Shevuot. And Ribam explains that it is not difficult at all, for this is what is stated there: Rava said to him, "What is the superiority [of this approach]? If so, the oath of bailees, which the Merciful One obligated — how can it ever be found? Since he could have said, 'There was never any such matter,' he could [also] say, 'It was lost through circumstances beyond my control'!" [The Gemara answers:] Where [the owner] deposited it with him before witnesses. [Rava objects:] Even where he deposited it before witnesses, since he could say, 'I returned it to you,' he could [also] say, 'It was lost through circumstances beyond my control'! [The Gemara answers:] Where he deposited it with him by means of a document. Explanation: Since he deposited it with him by means of a document, there is an oath in the case of 'it was lost through circumstances beyond my control,' for then one cannot say, 'Since he could have said, "I returned it to you,"' and [thereby] he would be believed without an oath — for one who deposits with another by means of a document, [the bailee] must return it to him before witnesses; and by strict law he would not be believed even with an oath, were it not that he is believed [with an oath] by virtue of the migo of 'it was lost through circumstances beyond my control.' And now there is nothing to ask from there.
